rationale: The claims_unverified revalidator is a ladder of 18 arms ending in three gates that stand between a clean scan and closing a human-review item about an unsupported factual claim. Those three gates have never been observed doing anything, and the three verdict counters (resolved/still_holds/unknown) structurally cannot say why. On 2026-08-13 the daily sweep decided 21 items with every gate refusal counter at 0; the true cause was that a clean scan happened 0 times in 21, so no gate was ever consulted. That was only discoverable by LIKE-matching the prose of result.revalidation.reason. Over two days the same zero carried four different meanings — never shipped, shipped but never asked, asked and approved, and the code ran but the ladder stopped above the gate — and no count could distinguish them. This change records WHICH RUNG DECIDED as a stable key, result.revalidation.arm, so the question becomes a GROUP BY instead of a prose match. It is pure instrumentation: no arm is added, removed or reordered, no predicate changes, and nothing branches on the new field. The point is that a refusal counter can only ever observe one of a gate's two outcomes, while 'was this gate reached at all' is the question that was actually being asked and could not be answered.
submitter: bugfix_168_deployed_asset_path (retraction lane) — answering the open question left by the 2026-08-13 sweep: how would we ever observe these three gates?

plan.summary: Add an observation-only `arm` key to the revalidation record: a stable name for the ladder rung that decided. Instrument the 18 arms of the claims_unverified revalidator; record `unreported:<item_type>` for the four revalidators not yet instrumented so a gap cannot read as an absence. No behavioural change.

edits.rationale: The struct is the shared seam every revalidator returns. Arm is additive, `json:"arm,omitempty"`, and no existing revalidator is required to set it. The doc comment states the property the field is queried on and the one rule that keeps it trustworthy: nothing may ever branch on it, because an instrument that changes the outcome it measures cannot then be evidence about that outcome.

Four of the five registered revalidators do not name their arms today. Writing an empty string for those would make 'this revalidator is uninstrumented' and 'no rung was reached' the same query result — the exact conflation the ladders themselves are built to avoid. recordedArm writes `unreported:<item_type>` instead, so the gap names itself. It is a function rather than three inline lines for the same reason unverifiedClaimsVerdict is split from its query glue: the rule is then testable without a database, and a rule stated only in a comment is enforced by nothing.

edits.symbol: arm name constants + all 18 return sites
edits.rationale: One named constant per return site, set at each. The `gate_` prefix is the load-bearing part: any arm carrying it proves the scan came back clean and a gate was CONSULTED, which is the observation a refusal counter cannot give, since a gate that refuses and a gate never asked both report nothing. The gates are named for what they check rather than numbered, because the ladder consults them (claims, copy, published) in a different order from the one they were built in, so any numbering would have encoded one order and misled about the other.

The arm is queried, which makes it a contract. The test drives 14 real fixtures through the ladder rather than listing the constants against themselves, so it fails on a copy-pasted arm name: it pins reachability, pairwise distinctness (two rungs sharing a name merge into one GROUP BY bucket and the merged count still looks plausible), and the reach predicate exactly as the SQL runs it. Four mutations were run against it — duplicate arm name, a gate arm stripped of its prefix, a return site with no arm, and recordedArm returning empty — and each failed the specific assertion written for it, with the restored code green.

grounded_in: Live clients_db, 2026-08-13: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE result #>> '{revalidation,reason}' LIKE '%register moved, not the page%'), … over item_type='claims_unverified' AND result ? 'revalidation' returns refused_gate1=0, refused_gate2=0, refused_gate3=0, resolved=9, still_holds=18, unknown=3, total=30. All three gate refusal counters are zero and have always been zero.

The 2026-08-13T08:44:39Z sweep decided 21 items and not one reached a gate. From the verdicts' own reasons: 18 still_holds ('page X still carries N claim(s) the register does not support'), 2 unknown (page absent or no readable content), 1 unknown (site has no evidence_base spec). The gates sit downstream of a clean scan and a clean scan happened 0 times in 21.

Ordering verified rather than assumed: that run executed against v1.0.1293, which carries all three gates (1293 rolled 2026-08-12 19:13:54Z; 1295 only at 2026-08-13 13:53:19Z), so 08:44:39Z sits inside 1293's window. The zero is a real result, not an artefact of an old binary.

revalidate_unverified_claims.go's own ladder shows why a counter cannot answer this: the three gates are the LAST arms, after `if len(scan.Findings) > 0 { return still_holds }`. An item whose page still trips the check returns before any gate is consulted, and the gate's counter reads 0 in exactly the same way as a gate that was asked and approved.

The load-bearing invariant is unchanged by this edit and re-measured after it: every closure still shows the copy moved — (newest_component_update > item_filed_at) is `t` for 9 of 9 resolved items, 0 rows false.

Self-caught during implementation, and it is the reason the test asserts a predicate rather than a prefix: the first version checked `HasPrefix(arm, "gate_")` and failed on `resolved_all_gates_passed`, the one arm that proves all three gates were reached AND passed. A prefix-only reach query would have counted only the reaches where a gate REFUSED and missed every closure — the same two-opposite-causes trap this field exists to close, reproduced inside the instrument on its first run.
plan.risks: The field is partially populated by design: only revalidateUnverifiedClaims names its arms, so voice_tells, needs_page and the two named-field types will record `unreported:<item_type>`. That is deliberate and self-describing rather than a NULL, but a reader who filters `arm LIKE 'gate_%'` fleet-wide will see one revalidator's rungs and must not read the others' absence as 'no gate was reached'. Lifting arms into the other revalidators is tracked with the shared-helper work in features_open/032. The arm names are a queried vocabulary, so renaming one silently zeroes whatever was counting it. The const block says add, never rename; nothing enforces that mechanically. This makes the gates observable; it does NOT make them observed. Nothing in the current population produces a clean scan, so the expected first result is 21 rows of scan_still_trips and zero gate rows — which is the instrument working, not the gates approving. The separate question of whether any item can ever reach a gate is a population problem, not an instrumentation one, and is left open for the owner. One extra jsonb key per decided item per day. No index, no new query in the hot path, no additional read.
